title: Aerrow
dek: A scout who seeks freedom through strength, learns the cost of overreaching in Babel’s wilds and helps turn dangerous journeys into supplies for the Refuge.

facts.Account: Surviving testimony; exact in-world date unresolved
facts.February hunt: Two deaths; Arjahn’s first Revivify is followed by a second death and later restoration by Elenia

sources: Babel quest record · refuge warning, June 2026

body:
Aerrow is a Shadar-kai sorcerer and scout whose work in Babel-Ashur joins reconnaissance, gathering and dangerous hunts. He seeks physical perfection and resists the servitude he associates with his people, yet learns to rely on companions whose skills differ from his own.

Aerrow is present at Skylight Refuge when the adventurers regroup. Worn down and startled by the sounds of enormous beasts, he reports finding slain natives while searching for food. He describes monsters drawing nearer to the caves and fears that the shadow from the tunnels is searching for the refuge.

His warning helps turn the group’s attention toward making contact with the people of Babel. He later suggests the hunters may be searching for a seed, while acknowledging that this could be his imagination. These are Aerrow’s reports and fears, not proof that he witnessed every enemy movement or knows the hunters’ full plans.

Recognizing another warrior

Aerrow and Aravil meet while practicing at the range. He calls her an ally and speaks of feeling slow after his arrival; she says she is finally finding her stride. They recognize a shared longing for the front. The exchange records their affinity without making either character’s judgments universal.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4.

January · gathering is dangerous work

Aerrow joins Aravil and Arjahn in searching beyond the Refuge for the resources a lasting camp needs. He admits how poorly he reads the unfamiliar jungle, follows Aravil’s quieter path and proposes equipment that might help future journeys. The first outing yields buried carvings and components from defeated creatures; it does not yield an explanation of the lost civilization.

The larger company then fights an aqualisk and demodragons. Aerrow is badly hurt before Eugene finishes the aqualisk. Healing restores his body faster than he can make sense of the experience. His appetite for glory coexists with caution: he urges the hunters to gather quickly, leave the carcasses and return with materials for the builders. A later hunt with Eugene and Aravil includes an escape from an unidentified threat and a hard-won serpent kill whose harvest fails.

February · a return that does not last

With Aravil missing, Aerrow goes out with Arjahn to find supplies for a safer shelter. He tries to keep his angry companion focused on the job rather than revenge. Arjahn agrees not to pursue danger at the cost of Aerrow’s life, but an aqualisk and its accompanying demodragons overwhelm the pair.

The combat record shows Aerrow dying, Arjahn casting Revivify and Aerrow returning with a single point of life. Renewed attacks kill him again. Arjahn escapes with his body, bringing him back to the cave through repeated magical jumps. This temporary Revivify must remain distinct from the later restoration after the retreat.

A companion brought home, and a warning heard

The main Babel quest later finds Arjahn beside Aerrow’s preserved body. Arjahn says he withheld his only powerful diamond and judges that choice harshly. Elenia calls for aid and the scene explicitly describes her raising the scout. The checked passage does not name her spell. Arjahn’s self-blame records his moral crisis rather than proving that he caused every danger the hunters faced.

Aerrow’s later warning at the Refuge therefore comes from someone who has already suffered the wilderness’s cost. His report of slain natives and approaching monsters deserves attention without making his suspicions about every enemy plan certain. Follow the hunts, their losses and the work they support →

    Learning to use another hunter’s strengths

    Aerrow follows Aravil’s stealth, helps search for useful materials and urges the party to leave exposed battle sites.

    The group is unfamiliar with Babel’s ecology.
    Consequence
    Their different skills make a supply journey possible.
    Still unresolved
    Buried carvings do not identify their makers; harvested components do not complete the camp.

    A healed body is not an untroubled mind

    After the aqualisk nearly breaks his body, Aerrow says he feels physically well but is still struggling with the memory.

    Known at this stage
    Arjahn’s healing has repaired the immediate injuries.
    Consequence
    Survival still requires time and attention after the fight.
    Still unresolved
    This is his immediate experience, not a diagnosis or a completed recovery.

  3. 2026-02-06 · quest

    Two deaths, one temporary Revivify

    Aerrow dies during the two-person hunt, returns through Arjahn’s Revivify and is killed again before the retreat.

    Known at this stage
    The escape is taking place under continued attack.
    Consequence
    Arjahn carries his body back; the final restoration happens in the later quest scene.
    Still unresolved
    Elenia’s later raising is shown without a named spell in the checked passage.
